name: Ezra
overview: Ezra was a male figure who played a pivotal role in the history of Judah by returning to the land after the Babylonian captivity, as noted in Nehemiah 7:7. Although his tribal affiliation is not specified, his identity is marked by this significant return. It is noteworthy that the name Ezra does not appear in the traditional BHS Hebrew text but is found in the Rahlfs Septuagint, highlighting textual variations in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Ezra appears as a proper name in Nehemiah 7:7 without a given meaning or divine naming indicated. There are no additional titles or meanings provided for this name in the biblical record referenced.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Ezra beyond what is stated about his return to Judah after captivity. There are no listed relatives or connections in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Ezra is significant in the biblical narrative as a priest and scribe who led the second group of exiles back to Jerusalem, demonstrating deep commitment to God's Law. His leadership in religious reform restored the centrality of Scripture and proper worship among the post-exilic Jewish community. Through confronting issues like intermarriage with pagan peoples and guiding the people to repentance, Ezra helped preserve Jewish identity and foreshadowed the New Testament emphasis on spiritual purity and adherence to God's Word.
